candidates.tagline: Valve promised 4K 60fps — then quietly deleted that promise
candidates.story: The $1,049 Valve Steam Machine launched June 22, 2026 with '4K gaming at 60 FPS' prominently on its store page; after reviews showed most AAA games couldn't hit that target even on medium settings, Valve silently changed the claim to 'up to 4K gaming with FSR 4.1' on June 25.
candidates.why_funny: Valve spent years over-promising 4K 60fps performance and, when reviewers proved it wrong in real games, solved the controversy by just deleting the claim from the store page.
candidates.alt: Dark navy blue Steam Machine gaming PC cube sitting on a wood desk next to a monitor showing a colorful game, with two small decorative mushroom figurines beside it

candidates.tagline: The Coca-Cola ad display that ran out of space to advertise
candidates.story: A Coca-Cola branded advertising display in a supermarket in São Miguel, Azores was running Ubuntu, and when the volume 'storage' dropped to 201.5 MB remaining, the Ubuntu 'Low Disk Space' dialog box interrupted the branded display with two options: 'Examine...' or 'Ignore.'
candidates.why_funny: Coca-Cola's billion-dollar brand machine forgot to clear the logs on its fancy digital signage, exposing the unglamorous Ubuntu desktop to every shopper in the Azores.
candidates.alt: Bright red Coca-Cola branded advertising display in a Portuguese supermarket with a Ubuntu 'Low Disk Space' dialog box reading 'The volume storage has only 201,5 MB disk space remaining' centered over the Coca-Cola bottle cap logo, with Coca-Cola cans on shelves visible at left
